litematica.litematica.config.comment.betterrenderor:
If enabled, then the schematic rendering is done by injecting the different render call into the vanilla rendering code.

This should result in better translucent block rendering/ordering and schematic blocks not getting rendered through the client world blocks/terrain.

If the rendering doesn't work (for example with Optifine), then try disabling this option. But in most cases you want to keep this enabled.
litematica.litematica.config.comment.blockinfolines: If enabled, then a MiniHUD-style small §fBlock Info Lines HUD§r is rendered for the looked-at block (by default in the top right corner of the screen).

litematica.litematica.config.comment.blockinfooverl: Enables the §fBlock Info Overlay§r rendering, while holding the §eRender Info Overlay§r hotkey.\n\nThe §fBlock Info Overlay§r will show the expected and/or found block's name and block state properties, and also a preview of the inventory contents, for the block yo uare looking at.
The alignment of the §fBlock Info Overlay§r HUD
The y-offset of the §fBlock Info Overlay§r from the selected screen edge
litematica.litematica.config.comment.changeselected:
If enabled, then the "element selection" of an area selection is always set to the last moved corner, when using the set corner hotkeys (Hotkeys -> §eSet Selection Box Corner [1 | 2]§r).

The selected element is what the tool item and some hotkeys will control/move. This is basically the same as using the §eTool Select Elements§r key (by default middle click) with the tool on the moved corner to select it.

§dTL;DR;§r Always select the corner that was just moved (for example by left/right clicking with the tool).
litematica.litematica.config.comment.cloneatorigina: If enabled, then using the §eClone Selection§r hotkey will create the placement at the original area selection's position, instead of at the player's current position
litematica.litematica.config.comment.commandnameset:
The §a/setblock§r equivalent command name to use for the §fPaste Schematic§r feature for the command-based §fPaste§r mode.

§6Note:§r The command arguments must match the vanilla setblock command, i.e. §a <x> <y> <z> <block>§r.

The command-based §fPaste§r mode is used on servers that don't have proper server-side support for Litematica creative mode features.
litematica.litematica.config.comment.customschemati: Allows using a custom schematic directory location. This for example allows you to use the same schematic directory for several different Minecraft instances.\n\nNormally the main schematic directory is at §a'.minecraft/schematics/'§r, but this allows you to select another location for it, for example in your Dropbox/Google Drive folder or just some other common location anywhere on your system.
litematica.litematica.config.comment.dateformat:
A date format pattern for the date and time shown in some tooltips and info panels.

This should be a valid Java §eSimpleDateFormat§r pattern.
See: §9https://docs.oracle.com/javase/7/docs/api/java/text/SimpleDateFormat.html§r
litematica.litematica.config.comment.debugmessages: Enables some debug messages in the game console
litematica.litematica.config.comment.defaultareasel: The default Area Selection mode for any new worlds that don't have it saved in the per-world config file yet
litematica.litematica.config.comment.easyplaceclick: If enabled, then the §fEasy Place§r mode will always try to click on existing adjacent blocks. This may help on Spigot or similar servers, which don't allow clicking on air blocks.
litematica.litematica.config.comment.easyplacehold: Allows you to just hold down the use key (right click) and look at different schematic blocks to place them, when using the §fEasy Place§r mode. Without this option you need to separately click on each block.
litematica.litematica.config.comment.easyplacemode: The main on/off switch for §fEasy Place§r: right click a schematic block to place the right block there.\n\n§6Note:§r If you want to just hold down right click and walk around, then also enable the §eEasy Place Hold§r option.
litematica.litematica.config.comment.easyplacewarni: Whether to show the §a"Action prevented by *"§r warnings for the §fEasy Place§r and §fPlacement Restriction§r modes
litematica.litematica.config.comment.executerequire: Require holding an enabled tool item for the §eExecute Operation§r hotkey to work.\n\nSee the description of the Hotkeys -> §eExecute Operation§r hotkey for more info.
litematica.litematica.config.comment.fixrailrotatio: Applies a fix for the vanilla bug in the rail rotation method, where the 180 degree rotations of straight north-south and east-west rails rotate 90 degrees counter-clockwise instead >_>
litematica.litematica.config.comment.generatelowerc: If enabled, then by default the suggested schematic file names in the name text field of the save schematic screen will be lowercased and using underscores in place of spaces or other "special" characters
litematica.litematica.config.comment.ignoreexisting:
If enabled, then any fluid blocks are ignored as "extra blocks" and as "wrong blocks", i.e. where the schematic has air or other blocks respectively.

Basically this makes building stuff under water a whole lot less annoying.

§6Note:§r You will most likely also want to enable the §eRender Colliding Schematic Blocks§r option at the same time, to allow the schematic blocks to be rendered over existing blocks.
litematica.litematica.config.comment.infohudalignme: The alignment of the §fInfo HUD§r, used for the §fMaterial List§r, §fSchematic Verifier§r highlight positions, unseen chunks messages when tasks are running etc.
litematica.litematica.config.comment.infohudmaxline: The maximum number of lines to show at once on the various §fInfo HUDs§r
litematica.litematica.config.comment.infohudoffset: The offset of the §fInfo HUD§r from the screen edge
litematica.litematica.config.comment.infohudscale: Scale factor for the §fInfo HUD§r rendering
litematica.litematica.config.comment.loadentiresche: If enabled, then the entire schematic is always loaded at once to the schematic world. If disabled, then only the part that is within the client's view distance is loaded.\n\n§eNOTE:§r Normally in pretty much all cases you want to keep this disabled!
litematica.litematica.config.comment.mainrenderingt: This is the mod main rendering toggle option.\n\nThis enables/disables §ball rendering§r in the mod.
litematica.litematica.config.comment.materiallistfr: When enabled, the schematic-based Material List is fetched directly from the block state container.\n\n§eNormally you want this.§r Only disable this if there is an issue where it gets the materials wrong for some reason (and then also report the issue and send the affected schematic in the issue report).
litematica.litematica.config.comment.materiallisthu: The color of the item count text in the Material List info HUD
The maximum number of items to show at once on the §fMaterial List HUD§r
Scale factor for the §fMaterial List HUD§r
Whether or not the number of stacks should be shown on the §fMaterial List HUD§r, or only the total number of items
litematica.litematica.config.comment.materiallistig:
Ignore the exact block state when generating material lists.

This may be useful for example for redstone components where the block state may be different while building or constantly changing.

§eWarning:§r Be aware that this might ignore more than you want in MC versions before 1.13!! (Because of "magic metadata" and block states that also contain the block type for a number of blocks.)

§eSo use with caution in 1.12.2 or lower versions!§r
litematica.litematica.config.comment.materiallistsl: Highlight inventory slots containing items that are currently missing or running low in the player's inventory, according to the currently active §fMaterial List§r
The color for the "completely out" slot highlight
The color for the "not enough" slot highlight
The color for the "less than one stack available" slot highlight
litematica.litematica.config.comment.overlayreduced: If enabled, then the adjacent/touching inner sides of the block overlays are removed/not rendered.\n\n§6Note:§r This is currently still unfinished and somewhat buggy especially at the render layer boundaries, but this can still be a big help with large schematics that have tons of overlay being rendered.
litematica.litematica.config.comment.pastecommandin: The task execution interval in game ticks the §fPaste Schematic§r task will run at in the command-based mode on servers.\n\nThe command-based §fPaste§r mode is used on servers that don't have proper server-side support for Litematica creative mode features.
litematica.litematica.config.comment.pastecommandli: Maximum number of commands to send per game tick, when using the §fPaste, Fill, Delete§r etc. features in the command-based mode on servers.\n\nThe command-based modes are used on servers that don't have proper server-side support for the Litematica creative mode features.
litematica.litematica.config.comment.pastereplacebe:
The block replace behavior for the Paste Schematic feature.
- §3None:§r Don't replace any existing blocks
- §3With non-air:§r Only "actual" (non-air) blocks
  from the schematic will replace existing blocks
- §3All:§r Everything from the schematic will replace
  existing blocks.

The difference between §3With non-air§r and §3All§r is whether or not air from the schematic will carve away existing blocks from the world. So if you for example want to paste something under water without making a cube of air around it, then use §3With non-air§r.

§6Tip:§r You can quickly cycle this value with the Hotkeys -> §eSub Mode Cycle§r hotkey while in the Paste mode.
litematica.litematica.config.comment.pickblock: Enables the schematic pick block features (§ePick Block Auto§r, if enabled, and the §ePick Block First§r and §ePick Block Last§r hotkeys.)
litematica.litematica.config.comment.pickblockauto:
Automatically do a pick block from the schematic before placing a block.

This is basically a better and fully automatic version of the §ePick Block Last§r hotkey, and this also works if you hold down the §eUse§r key (normally right click) to place many blocks.

Note that §ePick Block Enabled§r is still required for §bany§r of the "normal" schematic pick block feature to work (excluding the §fEasy Place§r mode, which has its own separate options).
litematica.litematica.config.comment.pickblockavoid: Any pick block actions will avoid replacing any damageable items in the hotbar
Any pick block actions will avoid replacing any tool items in the hotbar.\n\nThis means any items that extend the vanilla ToolItem class.
litematica.litematica.config.comment.pickblockignor: Ignores the NBT data on the expected vs. found items for pick block. Allows the pick block to work for example with renamed items.
litematica.litematica.config.comment.pickblockshulk: If the required item for pick block is not found in the player's inventory, but there is a Shulker Box that has the item, then that Shulker Box is moved to the player's hand instead.
litematica.litematica.config.comment.pickblockusabl:
The hotbar slots that are allowed to be used for the schematic pick block features.

Can use comma separated individual slots and dash separated slot ranges (no spaces anywhere).
Example: §a1,3,5-7,9
litematica.litematica.config.comment.placementbound: Enable Schematic Placement (sub-region) bounding box rendering
litematica.litematica.config.comment.placementboxsi: Enable Schematic Placement sub-region box side quads rendering, and set the alpha (opacity) of the sides
litematica.litematica.config.comment.placementenclo: Enable rendering the side quads for the enclosing box around a schematic placement, and set the alpha value (opacity) of the sides
litematica.litematica.config.comment.placementinfro: When enabled, created or moved placements are positioned so that they are fully infront of the player, instead of the placement's origin point being at the player's location
litematica.litematica.config.comment.placementrestr:
When enabled, blocks can only be placed exactly like and where the schematic says they should be. This restriction also prevents placing any blocks within 2 blocks of any schematic placement sub-regions.

In other words this feature tries to prevent any wrongly or accidentally placed blocks near any schematics. This may in some cases be useful to avoid accidents near delicate redstone contraptions etc.

§6Note:§r The §fEasy Place§r mode automatically uses basically this same feature/code internally.
litematica.litematica.config.comment.rendercollidin: Enable rendering the expected block in the schematic at the hovered/targeted block, if it's not currently correct

Enabled rendering the schematic blocks even when there is already an existing (wrong) block in the client world.

This is useful when trying to build something where there are for example snow layers or water in the way, or if you want to see the expected block instead of what is currently placed in the world.

Note that the §eRender Colliding Block at Cursor§r option might be a better alternative, depending on the situation.
litematica.litematica.config.comment.rendermaterial: Whether or not the §fMaterial List HUD§r should be rendered behind GUIs, i.e. while any GUIs are open
litematica.litematica.config.comment.renderthreadno: Removes the timeout from the rendering worker threads.\n\nIf you get very stuttery rendering when moving around or dealing with large schematics, try disabling this. It will however make the schematic (re-)rendering a lot slower in some cases (which means that newly loaded chunks or changes to the schmematic will get processed slower).
litematica.litematica.config.comment.requireadjacen: Whether the adjacent chunks around the target chunk need to be loaded for it to get processed.\n\nThis mostly affects whether you can use the Schematic Verifier next to missing chunks. This is mostly only useful when working on very technical projects that require working next to empty/missing/non-synced-to-client chunks.
litematica.litematica.config.comment.schematicblock:
Enable schematic §bblock§r rendering.

Disabling this allows you to only see the colored overlay, which may be useful for example when clearing out an area before starting to build.

In that use case you would usually also want to disable the missing block overlay as well (§eSchematic Overlay Type Missing§r), so that you don't have stuff at your face, but instead only an overlay around the blocks that you need to remove.
litematica.litematica.config.comment.schematicbrows:
The "extra" columns that should be enabled by default in all the schematic browser screens.

These columns can also be toggled temporarily by right clicking on the list widget, but not on a list entry, so for example by right clicking on the header widget/search bar area.

Note: The file name column is always enabled.

litematica.litematica.config.comment.schematiceditr: The color of Edit Schematic mode's replace selector overlay

litematica.litematica.config.comment.schematicrende: Enable rendering the schematic and the overlay.\n\nThis turns off the entire schematic rendering, but allows other things like the placement bounding boxes and the info HUDs to still render.
litematica.litematica.config.comment.schematicverif: Forces using blocks models for everything in the Schematic Verifier result list.\n\nNormally item models are used for anything that has an item, and block models are only used for blocks that don't have an item, plus for Flower Pots to see the contained plant.
litematica.litematica.config.comment.showextraschem: Show all the extra/uncommon schematic types as available save targets. These are always supported for loading files, but are hidden by default from the schematic type selection dropdown widget when saving schematics.
litematica.litematica.config.comment.shownewuserext: Show extra nags/reminders for new users
litematica.litematica.config.comment.showreminderdi: Show an extra message with the nag messages on how to turn the nag messages off
litematica.litematica.config.comment.signtextpaste: Automatically add the stored sign text from the schematic to the sign GUI when placing a sign
litematica.litematica.config.comment.statusinfohud: Enable a §fStatus Info HUD§r renderer, which renders a few bits of status info, such as the current Render Layer mode and the various renderers' enabled state.\n\nThis basically gives you a quick overview of what rendering things are enabled or disabled.
litematica.litematica.config.comment.statusinfohuda: Allow automatically momentarily enabling the §fStatus Info HUD§r "when needed", for example when creating a new placement while having rendering disabled
litematica.litematica.config.comment.toolhudalignme: The alignment of the §fTool HUD§r, when holding the configured "tool item"
litematica.litematica.config.comment.toolhudalwaysv: Whether or not the §fTool HUD§r should always be rendered, even when not holding the tool item
litematica.litematica.config.comment.toolhudoffset: The offset of the §fTool HUD§r from the screen edge
litematica.litematica.config.comment.toolitem:
The item to use as the "tool item" for the mod actions such as controlling area selection boxes.

§6Tip:§r You can use an empty hand as the "tool" by leaving this textfield empty or putting in the literal word §aempty§r.

By default the item check ignores NBT data, but if you for some reason want to use a special (for example renamed) item as the tool, you can append the required NBT tags and their values after the item name and metadata, like: §aminecraft:stick@0{display:{name:"Foo Bar"}}§r.

However in most cases I would recommend just using whatever item you always have on you, and toggle the tool functionality ON/OFF as needed using the §eTool Item Functionality§r config or hotkey. Dealing with "special items" is just pointless extra effort and annoyance and wasted inventory space in my opinion.
litematica.litematica.config.comment.toolitemenable:
If enabled, then the "tool item" can be used to control area selections, placements etc.

You can toggle this ON/OFF as needed to be able to use for example your regular food item as the tool, so that you don't need to carry around unnecessary extra items like sticks.

See Hotkeys -> §eTool Set Primary/Secondary Position§r and §eTool Select *§r etc. for the related hotkeys and modifier hotkeys that are used while holding the "tool item".
litematica.litematica.config.comment.toolselectionm:
The tool item behavior mode for any area selections.

In the §3Corners§r mode you left click to set the primary corner and right click to set the secondary corner.

In the §3Expand§r mode you right click to reset/collapse the selection box to the clicked position, and then you left click to expand the selection around all the clicked points.

§6Tip:§r The §3Expand§r mode is almost always superior, the only downside being that it can't shrink by clicking (other than fully collapsing the selection). Because there is always a block somewhere at each side of the build you want to select, you can always use the §3Expand§r mode to select anything, while in the §3Corners§r mode you often don't have a block at the opposite corners of the build, which would require using annoying temporary blocks.

§6TL;DR;§r Use the §3Expand§r mode, it's much more Pog ;)

§6Tip:§r You can quickly cycle this value with the Hotkeys -> §eSub Mode Cycle§r hotkey while in any tool mode that uses area selections.
litematica.litematica.config.comment.translucentblo: When enabled, then the "inner" block model sides that would normally be obstructed/not visible are also rendered, if §eTranslucent Schematic Rendering§r is enabled.
litematica.litematica.config.comment.translucentsch: Enables translucent schematic rendering, and sets the alpha value (opacity) of the rendered blocks.\n\§b0.0§r = completely transparent\n§b1.0§r = completely opaque

litematica.litematica.hotkey.comment.addselectionbo:
Add a new area selection sub-region box to the player's current position.

§6Note 1:§r This is only for the §fMulti-Region§r Area Selection mode. The §fSimple§r mode always just has one constant box, you can't remove it or add more.

§6Note 2:§r This hotkey shouldn't normally be needed, as the §fArea Editor§r menu should normally be preferred for creating and renaming and managing the sub-regions in a selection.
litematica.litematica.hotkey.comment.cloneselection: Quickly clone the current area selection. This basically just creates an in-memory-only schematic, and then creates a placement of that schematic and selects it, and also switches the tool mode to the §aPaste Schematic in World§r mode. You can then easily paste that "cloned selection" somewhere.\n\nAlso see the Generic -> §eClone at Original Position§r option, which controls if the created placement will be placed overlapping the original selection, or at the player's current location. Furthermore, the Generic -> §ePlacement Infront of Player§r option controls if the placement (in case it's created at the player's position) will be created "fully infront of the player" or if the origin point will be placed at the player's position.

litematica.litematica.hotkey.comment.easyplaceactiv: Optional. litematica.litematica.hotkey.comment.executeoperati:
Execute the currently selected tool operation (§6Fill, Replace, Paste Schematic§r etc.) using the current area selection or schematic placement.

§6Note:§r The features this hotkey is controlling are Creative-only functionality.

For this hotkey to work, you need to be holding an "enabled tool item". That means that you need to:
- Hold the correct tool item set in Generic -> §eTool Item§r
- The Generic -> §eTool Enabled§r config has to be §aON§r
- The Visuals -> §eMain Rendering Toggle§r option has to be §aON§r

§6TL;DR;§r Basically you must be able to see the tool HUD on the bottom left corner of the screen while holding the tool item.

§6Note:§r There is an option in Generic -> §eExecute Require Holding Tool§r to disable the requirement to be holding the "tool item".

litematica.litematica.hotkey.comment.pickblocklast:
A key to pick block the last schematic block ray traced to, before the first (possible) client world block ray traced to.

Basically this would get you the item for the schematic block you could place against an existing block.

So basically binding this to the vanilla §eUse§r key (normally right click) would do an automatic pick block before placing the block. Note however that this would only work when clicking, not when holding down the key.

litematica.litematica.hotkey.comment.selectiongrow:
A hotkey to auto-grow the currently selected area selection box around any adjacent/diagonally connected blocks.

Basically what this does, is expand the selection box by one block on every side, and then check if that expansion on a given side contains at least some non-air blocks, and if it does, then that expansion is kept. This process is repeated as long as the expansion succeeds in at least one direction.

So you can't use this for things that are connected to the ground/walls/terrain in some way, as then the expansion just grows to cover all the loaded chunks around the player.

litematica.litematica.hover.button.area_editor.manu:
Enabling a manual origin allows you to define the origin point of the area selection in a custom location/offset in relation to the sub-regions.

The automatic origin point would be at the minimum coordinate of all the sub-regions. In other words if you were to create an enclosing box around all the sub-regions, the automatic origin is the minimum coordinate corner of that box.

Defining a manual origin is mostly useful if you want to be able to automatically load the schematic (or rather create the placement) in the correct/specific location while standing at a certain location.

Basically when you create a placement, the origin point is by default at the player's location. And the origin point of a placement is the same as the origin point of an area selection. (Not in absolute coordinates when creating a selection, but rather the relative positions of all the sub-regions.)

litematica.litematica.hover.button.schematic_save.s:
Where/how to save the schematic.

- Auto: Use server-side saving, if the server reports the capability to save schematics
- Client: Force saving on the client side, even if the server would also support server-side saving
- Server: Force trying to save on the server side, even if the server may not support it and didn't report the capability. If it doesn't support it, then nothing will happen.

This option is only relevant and available while playing on a server.\n\nLitematica always saves the schematic from the integrated server's server world while in single player, so that it has access to all the block entity and entity data etc.

This option chooses where the schematic is saved from.

The normal common behavior is to save from the normal vanilla Minecraft world.

It's also possible to save from the "Schematic World" (where all enabled schematic placements will place the schematic to for rendering and other technical reasons), or from a combination of both.

Saving from the schematic world allows you to create a new schematic from a loaded schematic without pasting it to a temporary world, if you for example want to only save a part of it, or combine parts of multiple loaded schematics into one.

The "A or B" options will first check the first world "A", and if it has an "air-like block" in a given position, then world "B" is checked. This allows you to for example save a new schematic of a build where the build is placed inside existing terrain.

litematica_upgraded.litematica_upgraded.config.comment.perfb: Built schematic pieces are grouped into bigger draw jobs, so the game makes far fewer draw calls each frame. The picture stays the same. Off by default: it saves no frame time on most PCs and can stutter while a schematic is being built.

litematica_upgraded.litematica_upgraded.config.comment.perfg: While you move a placement, its built chunks are drawn shifted without rebuilding; once it stays still the real rebuild runs in the background and replaces them.
litematica_upgraded.litematica_upgraded.config.comment.perfl: Glass, water and other see-through blocks are re-sorted only after you moved a real distance, not every frame.
litematica_upgraded.litematica_upgraded.config.comment.perfm: While you move a placement, a complete copy of it is drawn (also the blocks that already match the world), so it shows no holes. It is kept until you deselect the placement, so the next move shows it at once.

litematica_upgraded.litematica_upgraded.config.comment.perft: Chunks next to you are built on the background threads too, so standing inside a big placement does not stutter. Off: those chunks are built on the render thread, as stock Litematica does.

malilib.malilib.config.comment.configbackupantid:
The rotated config backups will be "anti-duplicated"

This means that if the to-be-created new config backup file is identical to an already existing older backup, then that older backup is moved as the latest backup, instead of creating a new backup.

Basically this prevents spamming new useless backups and overwriting older different backups if for example a single feature is toggled on and off often.

§8(The configs are saved to file any time the config menu is closed, and any configs have changed since last being saved. So for example toggling on or off a feature, and then opening and closing the config menu for that mod would cause the configs for that mod to get saved.)
malilib.malilib.config.comment.configbackupcount: This is the number of backup copies that will be kept of each of the mod config files.\n\nA new backup is created whenever the config file is written to, which normally happens after some configs have been modified and the config screen is closed, or when logging out of the world.

malilib.malilib.config.comment.configtooltipmaxl: The maximum number of tooltip lines to show by default.\n\nTooltips longer than this will be hidden by default, and will just show the §f§oHold §e§oShift§f§o for information§r text unless the Shift key is held.
malilib.malilib.config.comment.configwidgetbackg: Enables a background color for the config option widgets on the config screens.\n\nThis is by default a slightly different color for odd and even rows.
malilib.malilib.config.comment.configwritemethod:
The write "method" that is used for writing to the config files.

- §aNormal Write§r - malilib writes to the config file directly
- §aTemp and Rename§r - malilib writes to a temporary file first, and then renames the temporary file over the old file

§aNormal Write§r should work if you want to symlink or hard link the config files from some other location, whereas §aTemp and Rename§r in that case would just replace the <st>symlink</st> or hardlinked file and thus "break the link".

§aTemp and Rename§r on the other hand should be safer against config file corruption, if the game were to crash while the configs are being written to. But then again malilib now by default keeps backups of the config files anyway.

§dNote:§r This option is actually redundant for symlinks, as symlinks currently always use direct writing instead of temporary files and renaming. This is only needed if you use hardlinked config files.
malilib.malilib.config.comment.coordinatedecimal: Whether the number of decimal digits should be clamped in various coordinate fields, and how many digits should be kept.\n\nNote that the clamping doesn't necessarily affect the underlying precision of the stored value, if the value is never modified using the text field. You can also still input arbitrary precision using the text field. This config just clamps the value that gets printed to the text field.
malilib.malilib.config.comment.customhotbarmessa: This is the maximum number of concurrent messages that will be shown in the custom "action bar"/hot bar message renderer\n\nThat renderer is by default used to show the config option toggle messages etc.

malilib.malilib.config.comment.datadumpcsvdelimi: The column delimiter to use for CSV format data dumps\n\nAn example use case is Litematica's Material List, when written to file in the CSV format instead of the "ascii art table" format.
malilib.malilib.config.comment.debugmessages: Enables some debug messages to the game console
malilib.malilib.config.comment.defaulttogglemess: This is the default message output for any boolean config toggle messages, if the §eMessage Output§r option in the <c=eee>Advanced KeyBind Settings§r of the associated toggle hotkey is set to §3Default Toggle Output§r.\n\nBasically this allows you to change the toggle message output for <c=eee>all boolean toggle hotkeys§r at once, as long as the §eMessage Output§r option for them is set to §3Default Toggle Output§r.
malilib.malilib.config.comment.dropdownsearchtip: Should the DropDown widget search tip (about just starting to type to open the search) be shown.\n\nNote that this automatically turns off when you type in a DropDown widget to open the search.

malilib.malilib.config.comment.guidebug: When enabled, all GUI widgets will draw their outlines, and when hovered, also their position and dimension info and the widget class name.\n\nIf a key is set for Debug -> §eGUI Debug Key§r, then that key must be held for any of the debug rendering to happen.
malilib.malilib.config.comment.guidebugall: Makes all widgets render their debug outline, instead of only the hovered widget.\n\nThis is only a sub-option for the behavior when the §eGUI Debug§r option is enabled.

malilib.malilib.config.comment.guidebugpadding: Makes widgets that have padding values set render an outline for the padding.\n\nThis is only a sub-option for the behavior when the §eGUI Debug§r option is enabled.

Now if another key combination such as §6M + C§r triggers first, then when the §6M§r key is released, it won't trigger since another hotkey already triggered before it.

If enabled, then this keybind will only trigger if it's the first keybind to trigger with the key event that triggers it.\n\nThis is kind of similar to §3Exclusive§r, but it's per-pressed-key and does not need all keys to be released to trigger again.

malilib.malilib.config.comment.keybinddebug: Enables printing all key presses and held keys to the game console\n\nIf the §eKeyBind Debug In Action Bar§r and/or the §eKeyBind Debug Toast§r options are enabled, then the message also appears in those renderers.

That system allows you to define translation overrides in-game, without making or editing a resource pack. This basically allows you to easily tweak or change any display strings that come from the lang file, without having to edit them via a resource pack.
